audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Karma six of seven stages while the matchup wins 46.77% (packet flagged exactly this), AND the two layers disagreed on rows 3, 4 and 5: full read Skill/Skill/Veigar where content read Karma/Karma/Karma.
audit.why: Grounded in the kits: Baleful Strike reaches 1000 to Karma's 950 and costs 30 mana at rank 1 on a 6s cooldown, so there is no Karma poke dominance to hand her the middle rows; from 6 the Event Horizon into Primordial Burst chain is a genuine kill, and Primordial Burst scales with the target's MISSING health, which is exactly what Karma's chip-trade pattern leaves her at.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-2 Karma, row 3 Skill, rows 4-6 Veigar — proposed as one atomic group with the paired content win[N] edits and every matching why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second invitation' off Event Horizon, and no real cooldown appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Event Horizon is 20/18.5/17/15.5/14s. Baleful Strike is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s. Primordial Burst is 120/90/60s. Dark Matter has NO base cooldown in the kit text — Phenomenal Evil stacks reduce it.
audit.corrected: Real numbers into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d, phases[3].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction — that Primordial Burst increases based on the target's missing health — was never stated, while the page simultaneously told you to chip-trade and then sit in the lane.
audit.why: Riot text: 'dealing a large amount of magic damage, increasing based on the target's missing health.' Against a chipped Karma that R is a kill from 650. The correct sequencing is trade at full or not at all, and RE as the cage forms rather than after the burst starts.
audit.corrected: Stated in dontsFull[2].d, dosFull[1].d, phases[4].why, enemyWin and breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.after: Veigar wins by catching you on the cage edge, dropping Dark Matter, and finishing with a Primordial Burst that scales on the damage.

edits.after: Ahead, sprint: RQ him off the wave, deny the Baleful Strike stacks, take plates, and W-root him whenever Event Horizon is down.

edits.after: If Veigar opens the score, Phenomenal Evil is permanent AP that never comes back — stop contesting his stacks, farm at 950 with Q, and keep Mantra for RE the moment his cage forms.

edits.before: Carry early or enable late — RQ chips win lanes; RE + roots win the teamfights your early lead bought.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, and on real windows RQ-W: the chunk plus tether-root turns a poke trade into a kill setup — E out before the answer.
edits.after: His burst is cage, Dark Matter, then Primordial Burst — RE as the cage forms, because his R scales on the health the combo already took.

edits.before: Veigar burns Event Horizon (Cage) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.

edits.before: Your tether breaks if YOU walk away — holding the root means holding your ground for two seconds you must plan for.
